{"self_assessment": "Impact: My main contribution was the early call to draw a fish: a simple outline with a clear tail, which suits a judge who only sees fallen dominoes. After that, my direct impact was modest. Maya redrew the plan so everything grew from the start at the tail, and the table's build ran mostly through Maya, Leo and Tom. At the last check the outline was dark and connected, and about 151 of 196 standing dominoes should fall. The inner tail loop stayed pale, so it won't show. I don't know yet whether the judge will read it as a fish.

Execution: My early plan had the start at the nose, which was wrong, and Maya caught it and fixed it. I also asked for the pad when she already held it, which added some noise. When my assigned stroke overlapped with Maya's and Leo's work, I didn't push to take a piece of it. I stayed clear and didn't run any inspections during the long idle stretch, so I added little to verification. I should have picked up the nose joint or the tail forks and checked them myself.

Collaboration: I split the work early and deferred quickly once Maya took over the plan. I kept out of Leo's way while he worked on the tail diagonal and didn't risk a bump. I wasn't very visible in the middle of the activity, though, and I could have offered concrete help instead of only agreeing.

Leadership: I set the initial direction, then let Maya lead once she had the pad and the corrected plan. That was the right call for avoiding confusion, but I didn't step back in to share the load. Next time I'll claim a specific stroke or check early and say so, rather than waiting to be assigned."}
